title: VS Code Reference
description: A quick reminder of the ideas and examples in the VS Code lessons. Open the linked lesson when you need more help.

entries.name: An editor helps you write files
entries.summary: Visual Studio Code is a code editor. It helps you read and change files, but it is not the same thing as a browser or every language's runtime.

example.code:
Editor: write index.html
Browser: display index.html
Separate runtime: needed for languages such as Python

notes: Installing the editor does not install every programming language.

entries.name: Open a practice folder
entries.summary: Opening a folder gives the editor a workspace for related files. Use a new folder made only for learning.
notes: Do not open a sensitive or unfamiliar project and immediately trust or run all its tasks.

entries.name: Use the Command Palette
entries.summary: The Command Palette searches editor actions by name. It is useful when you do not remember a menu location.

example.code:
Open the Command Palette
Search: Format Document
Read the command name before choosing it

notes: Read a command before running it; similar names can do different things.

entries.name: Save and recognise file types
entries.summary: A file extension helps the editor choose language support. Saving changes writes them to disk; an unsaved tab can differ from the saved file.

example.code:
index.html -> HTML
style.css -> CSS
notes.txt -> plain text

notes: A file named page.html.txt is still a text file by its final extension.

entries.name: Search within a file
entries.summary: Find locates matching text in the current file. Check match-case and whole-word settings when results seem surprising.

example.code:
Text: Moon moon moonlight
Search: moon
Match case on: lowercase matches only
Whole word on: excludes moonlight

notes: An empty result can come from a filter, not from missing text.

entries.name: Search across the project
entries.summary: Workspace search finds text in several files. Review the included and excluded paths before trusting the result.

example.code:
Search target: club-site files
Query: Reading club
Possible matches: index.html and notes.txt

notes: Excluded or ignored files may not appear in search results.

entries.name: Replace with a preview
entries.summary: Replace changes text. Review each match or the preview before applying many changes at once.

example.code:
Old label: Save book
New label: Bookmark book
Review: check every matched file before replacing

notes: Do not run a broad replacement without reviewing its scope.

entries.name: Formatting keeps layout consistent
entries.summary: A formatter adjusts layout such as indentation. It should preserve the intended program behaviour. The formatter used depends on the language and setup.

example.code:
Before: const score={value:8};
After:  const score = { value: 8 };

notes: Formatting is not the same as fixing every program bug.

entries.name: Workspace settings
entries.summary: Workspace settings apply to the project. A .vscode/settings.json file can record a few agreed editor choices.
notes: Do not commit private paths or secrets into shared workspace settings.

entries.name: The integrated terminal
entries.summary: The integrated terminal is a real shell inside the editor window. Its commands can change files just like any other terminal.

example.code:
Read the current directory
Run a harmless version command if the tool is installed
Example: git --version

notes: Do not paste an unfamiliar command just because it is shown near editor instructions.

entries.name: Extensions and workspace trust
entries.summary: Extensions add editor features. Workspace Trust helps decide whether code in a folder may activate potentially risky features.

example.code:
New downloaded project
First: read its files in a restricted state
Then: trust only when you understand the source and needed actions

notes: An extension can have significant access; avoid installing random ones for every tutorial.

entries.name: Debug one step at a time
entries.summary: A debugger can pause a supported program and let you inspect values. A breakpoint marks a place to pause. Setup depends on the language runtime.

example.code:
Breakpoint before: total = price * count
Inspect: price is 3, count is 2
Step over: total becomes 6

notes: Do not confuse stepping through code with proving every input is correct.
